# Requirements traceability matrix

Derived line by line from [docs/splitstick-1.0-release-notes.md (rev. 5)](../docs/splitstick-1.0-release-notes.md).

Every requirement traces to a promise made in the release notes. 'source' names the section. Nothing here is invented: if the notes do not promise it, it is not a requirement.

**Generated — do not edit by hand.** Source of truth is `requirements/*.json`.
Regenerate with `npm run requirements`.

### Non-functional — 13

| ID | Requirement | Traces to | Verified by | Rel | M | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NFR-01` | **Low-overhead evidence capture** — Splitstick must add no more than 1 ms per event at p95 and 3 ms per event at p99 on a defined reference environment, measured over at least one million representative events across multiple benchmark runs. Measurements must include content commitment, encryption and local persistence, exclude deferred checkpoint and witness operations, and report sustained throughput and memory behaviour. The engineering stretch target remains p99 below 1 ms. Durability and integrity are never traded for latency: no deferring a critical write without guaranteed recovery, no weakening source-sequence or failure reporting, no removing encryption or commitment checks, and no uncontrolled buffering to improve a benchmark. | Numbers we are signing up to | Benchmark harness on the reference environment defined in bench/reference-env.json: p95 and p99 over at least 1e6 events, at least three repeats, reporting p50/p95/p99/p99.9, throughput, memory and GC activity. The harness declares each run an acceptance measurement or a regression metric and names every shortfall, and it verifies its own instruments — clock resolution and the GC recorder — in the same run. A run that meets p95 but not the p99 stretch target is a pass against the budget and is reported as such. | 1.0 | M1 | ☐ |
| `NFR-02` | **Run latency budget** — Added end-to-end agent run latency below 2%. | Numbers we are signing up to | Interleaved A/B through the real OMA orchestrator, analysed as a paired difference because the arms alternate run by run. The verdict requires the whole 95% interval to sit below the budget; a budget falling inside the interval is reported as UNRESOLVED rather than as a pass. The harness records its environment and checks its clock resolution. | 1.0 | M1 | ✅ |

Recording and anchoring are separate steps and separate runs: a statement recorded before any witness existed is anchored later against the checkpoint it already falls under.
